note: Reading notes shown in the app's 'About this diagram' panel. Explanatory text written for the app (Claude, 2026-11-06), not curated data; each note says where its claim comes from.

all.title: What the energies are
all.text: Energies come from a simple orbital-interaction model (orthogonal tight-binding, Harrison couplings). The starting atomic-orbital energies are the orbital potential energies tabulated in Miessler, Fischer & Tarr. They are in model units on an eV scale and give the order and rough size of levels. They are not predicted ionisation energies or a spectrum.

all.title: What the star means
all.text: A star (σ*, π*) marks a level whose atom–atom contacts add up to destabilising in this model. It is computed from the orbital, not copied from a textbook, so it can differ from the usual label for levels that are nearly nonbonding.

has_hydrogen.title: Couplings to hydrogen
has_hydrogen.text: Harrison's coupling formula was never fitted to hydrogen. Couplings involving H are scaled by 0.6 so that the textbook level orderings come out right (DECISIONS.md B2). Treat those orderings as built in, not as independent evidence.

H2O lecture.title: Lecture simplification
H2O lecture.text: As in the lecture, O 2s is not allowed to mix with the hydrogens, so it stays nonbonding. Switch the Parameters toggle to Model to see what changes when it is allowed to mix: the lowest level drops and gains H character.

H2O model.title: Compare with the lecture
H2O model.text: Here O 2s is allowed to mix with the hydrogens. The Lecture setting of the Parameters toggle shows the slide's simplification, with O 2s nonbonding.

CH4.title: No H–H coupling
CH4.text: The model has no coupling between hydrogens, so the hydrogen combinations (a1 and t2) start at the same energy and the pairing stages of the construction are skipped.

BH3.title: The empty p orbital
BH3.text: B 2pz has no partner among the hydrogen combinations, so it stays nonbonding and empty. It is the LUMO: the Lewis-acid orbital.

SF6 model.title: Fluorine–fluorine contacts
SF6 model.text: Neighbouring fluorines (2.21 Å apart) and opposite fluorines (3.12 Å) both couple. The neighbouring contacts are what separate the eg combination from a1g. No sulfur d orbitals are used.

SF6 lecture.title: Same as the model
SF6 lecture.text: For SF6 the lecture preset is identical to the model; there is no separate simplification to switch off.

neutral H3.title: Partly filled degenerate level
neutral H3.text: Three electrons leave the e′ pair half-filled. The one-electron picture cannot say how they arrange, and the triangle would distort (Jahn–Teller). The diagram draws one arrangement only.

six H Oh.title: Teaching construction
six H Oh.text: Six hydrogens on the axes of an octahedron, with no central atom, to show the ligand group orbitals on their own. Four electrons partly fill t1u, so the occupation is not unique.

four H Td.title: Teaching construction
four H Td.text: CH4's four hydrogens without the carbon, with H–H coupling on, to show the a1 and t2 combinations and their split. Two electrons partly fill t2.

O2.title: Two unpaired electrons
O2.text: The last two electrons go into the πg* pair, one in each, as Hund's rule draws it. This matches O2's triplet ground state, but the one-electron model itself does not decide spin.

CO.title: The highest occupied level
CO.text: The HOMO is a σ level sitting mostly on carbon (98 %). Textbooks usually call it nonbonding, a carbon lone pair. In this model its contacts are very slightly destabilising (+0.38 eV), so it is drawn with a star. Both describe the same orbital.

allyl cation pi.title: Node on the middle carbon
allyl cation pi.text: The middle π level has zero coefficient on C2, so it is exactly nonbonding: the LUMO of the cation.

Si2.title: Period 3: what is compared
Si2.text: Only the ground-state spin is compared with experiment here (NIST CCCBDB). No orbital-ordering reference for period-3 diatomics is in the curated data yet, so the σg/πu order shown is the model's own. Only valence 3s and 3p orbitals are included; there are no 3d orbitals in this model.

Al2.title: Spin disagrees
Al2.text: Experiment gives Al2 a triplet ground state: the σg(3p) and πu levels lie so close that the two highest electrons stay unpaired. In this model σg(3p) sits about 1.7 eV below πu, so all six valence electrons pair up and the model predicts a closed shell. This is recorded as a disagreement, not adjusted (the same kind of failure as B2).
